title: The small tensor coproduct of field extensions is nontrivial
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $J$ be a small set [def-weil-size-convention]. For every $j\in J$ let $L_j/k$ be a field extension with structural embedding $a_j:k\to L_j$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $A$ be a coproduct of the commutative $k$-algebras $L_j$ in the category of commutative $k$-algebras (equivalently, the small tensor product $\bigotimes_{j\in J,k}L_j$), with its canonical maps $\iota_j:L_j\to A$. Then $A$ is nontrivial. This includes the empty family, for which $A$ is canonically $k$.

source.place: Tag 0CNJ, lemma-infinite-product-surjective, proof: choose a huge field extension containing all residue-field extensions; the finite-tensor/coproduct nontriviality is the algebraic core of that construction

proof.text: For every finite subset $S\subseteq J$, let $A_S=\bigotimes_{s\in S,k}L_s$. The finite-family tensor lemma [lem-trf-finite-family-tensor-nontrivial] says that $A_S$ is nontrivial, with $A_\varnothing=k$. If $S\subseteq T$, write $T=S\sqcup(T\setminus S)$ and identify $A_T$ with $A_S\otimes_k B_{S,T}$, where $B_{S,T}=\bigotimes_{t\in T\setminus S,k}L_t$. The structural map $k\to B_{S,T}$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal of the field $k$, and if it were all of $k$ then $1=0$ in the nontrivial ring $B_{S,T}$. Since $A_S$ is a $k$-vector space, it is flat; applying [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] to $k\hookrightarrow B_{S,T}$ gives that the canonical transition map $A_S\to A_T$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is injective. The empty-subset transition $k\to A_S$ is therefore injective as well.

proof.text: The finite subsets of $J$, ordered by inclusion, form a filtered index category. The categorical finite-subcoproduct theorem [lem-trf-family-coproduct-finite-filtered] identifies the coproduct $A$ with the filtered colimit of the $A_S$ and these transition maps. This identification is compatible with the canonical map from the empty finite subcoproduct $A_\varnothing=k$ to $A$.

proof.text: In a filtered colimit of rings presented by the disjoint union of the stages modulo the transition relations, equality of two elements from one stage means that their images agree at some later stage. Since every transition map above is injective, the images of $0$ and $1$ from the empty stage remain distinct at every later stage. Hence the canonical map $k=A_\varnothing\to A$ is injective, so $A$ is nontrivial. When $J=\varnothing$ the index has only the empty stage and the same conclusion says $A\cong k$.
